ci_runs.summary: All eight Windows/Linux, native/Java, base/Pinout jobs passed the 31-check setup and failed the first cold API VERIFY. The same five-cycle fixture reported rejected initial native wiring or an unexpected count of old PG wire identities. The restart loop stopped before its second and third VERIFY runs.
ci_runs.root_cause_analysis: Source investigation identified physical removal to AIR followed by replacement with the same API block/provider/slot before the deferred scan. ApiTerminals.queueReplacedSavedOwners compared the final block to the saved owner, saw no replacement, and could retain or reattach old saved PG IDs. Old entities restored before new placement caused duplicate placement rejection; old entities restored afterward left four identities where the fixture expected two. This causal explanation comes from source/reproduction investigation; the retained CI logs establish the eight observed failures.
ci_runs.corrective_work: Record physical removal durably before deferred scanning and retire the exact old wire identities; validate selected-source readiness. Corrective work is in progress and still requires a coherent packaged rebuild and all release gates.

success_appendices.observed_result: Both native and Java separate-JVM SETUP, ARM and VERIFY passed. Actual held saved PG wire references remained unbound before readiness; exact old PG/CEE identities were retired, replacements stayed at zero charge while isolated, and fresh wires in both systems powered them after readiness.
success_appendices.threading_correction: The trace explicitly reports serverThread=true and entityReady=false while the temporary thread name is entity-deserializer. Thread names alone do not prove worker-thread ownership, including in earlier candidate17 trace interpretation. The saved NBT readAdditionalSaveData -> setEndpoint2 -> makeWire call stack establishes binding before readiness; pinned EntityStorage.flush -> ProcessorMailbox.runAll explains synchronous server-thread deserialization. Readiness guarding is therefore needed in addition to actual server-thread ownership checks.
